items.title: Exercise 1.7: compact Euclidean log-Sobolev implies Poincaré

source.anchor: Exercise 1.7, printed p.43 / PDF p.55; compact Euclidean test classes and normalization in §2.1.1, printed pp.48–49 / PDF pp.60–61
source.attribution: Original ASTIS restatement and proof of the compact Euclidean implication. The exercise's abstract Chapter 1 form domain is not identified with this test class.

items.statement: Let μ be a Borel probability measure on a finite-dimensional complete real Hilbert space and let C be fixed. Suppose every compactly supported smooth real test v satisfies the function-form LSI with coefficient 2C. Then every compactly supported smooth real f satisfies variance at most C times its gradient energy. The integrability of f, its centered square and its squared gradient norm is part of the conclusion, not a premise. No centering of f or sign restriction on C is assumed. This is the compact Euclidean implication, not the closed-form or abstract semigroup statement.
assumptions: μ is a Borel probability on a finite-dimensional complete real Hilbert space, and C is a fixed real coefficient. Compact smooth inputs have genuine integrable mass, entropy integrand and gradient energy here; 0 log 0 is interpreted as zero.
For every compactly supported C-infinity real v, the homogeneous entropy of v² is bounded by 2C times its squared-gradient integral. The premise does not extend to arbitrary noncompact tests by fiat.
The target f is real, compactly supported and C-infinity, with no centering or supplied integrability. Compactness of the centered function is not assumed.

items.title: Exercise 1.7: the actual affine-law KL expansion (1.E.1)

source.anchor: Exercise 1.7 / (1.E.1), printed p.43 / PDF p.55; explicit consumer Corollary 2.1.2, printed p.50 / PDF p.62
source.attribution: Original ASTIS restatement and proof of the actual probability-law expansion, not copied textbook wording or the Corollary's transport proof.

items.statement: Let μ be a probability measure on a measurable space and f a real a.e. strongly measurable, a.e. uniformly bounded observable with zero μ-mean. Define the actual tilted measure by withDensity of the nonnegative-real image of 1+εf. For all sufficiently small real |ε|, including zero, this is a probability measure and its canonical extended-real KL relative to μ is finite. The real value of that finite KL is ε² times one half of the integral of f², plus a remainder that is little-o of ε² in the full neighborhood of zero.
assumptions: μ is a probability measure on an arbitrary measurable space; no geometry, finite-dimensionality or support assumption is used.

f is a.e. strongly measurable, |f| ≤ M a.e. for a fixed real M, and its integral is zero. Boundedness on the probability space gives integrability; the public conclusion derives positivity and mass one rather than assuming them.
Smallness is a two-sided real neighborhood, including ε=0. The affine density is implemented with ENNReal.ofReal; eventual a.e. positivity ensures this does not truncate the relevant density.

steps.title: Center without preserving support
steps.text: Compact support and continuity make f bounded and integrable. Probability normalization makes the centered function mean-zero. Subtracting a constant can destroy compact support of the function, but the derivative retains compact support.
steps.lean: integral_sub and fderiv_sub_const establish the two identities; hgsq is obtained from the actual bounded-function L² proof.

steps.title: Justify the noncompact square-root test
steps.text: For sufficiently small absolute parameter, bounded g makes the affine density lie between one half and three halves. Its square root is smooth. Mass and entropy integrands are integrable by boundedness, and the genuine gradient energy is integrable by the derivative formula and the compact support of Df. The previously proved cutoff extension, rather than the compact premise alone, makes this test legitimate.
steps.lean: eventually_contDiff_and_integrable_sqrt_perturbation produces the actual domains; the Riesz norm identity converts derivative to gradient; logSobolev_of_compact_smooth_tests applies the extension.

steps.title: Normalize and compensate
steps.text: The affine density has mass one. The homogeneous entropy normalization vanishes, and the integrated linear compensation also cancels. This step compares real integrals, not Radon–Nikodym laws.
steps.lean: hmass and hkl derive both cancellations from integrable terms.

steps.title: Divide by ε² and take the two limits
steps.text: For nonzero ε divide by its positive square. Taylor's integral remainder for k at 1 bounds its quotient by g² and gives pointwise limit g²/2. The energy quotient is bounded by half the squared gradient of g and tends to a quarter of it. Dominated convergence applies to both. Closedness of real order keeps the same constant; no division by C is used.
steps.lean: The compiled entropy and energy limit parents are independent; le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto gives the final comparison, and the Admissible conjunct uses the three established integrabilities.

units.lean_statement: Admissible is an output: integrability of the original observable, its centered square, and its squared gradient norm. The variance and energy definitions are exactly the displayed integrals.
units.lean_proof: Center the compact function, justify the true noncompact square-root domain, cancel the mass-one terms, and pass the scaled entropy and energy inequalities to the punctured limit.

units.title: Exercise 1.7: the actual affine-law KL expansion (1.E.1)
units.statement: Let μ be a probability measure on a measurable space and f a real a.e. strongly measurable, a.e. uniformly bounded observable with zero μ-mean. Define the actual tilted measure by withDensity of the nonnegative-real image of 1+εf. For all sufficiently small real |ε|, including zero, this is a probability measure and its canonical extended-real KL relative to μ is finite. The real value of that finite KL is ε² times one half of the integral of f², plus a remainder that is little-o of ε² in the full neighborhood of zero.
assumptions: μ is a probability measure on an arbitrary measurable space; no geometry, finite-dimensionality or support assumption is used.

f is a.e. strongly measurable, |f| ≤ M a.e. for a fixed real M, and its integral is zero. Boundedness on the probability space gives integrability; the public conclusion derives positivity and mass one rather than assuming them.
Smallness is a two-sided real neighborhood, including ε=0. The affine density is implemented with ENNReal.ofReal; eventual a.e. positivity ensures this does not truncate the relevant density.

steps.title: Construct the probability law
steps.text: Essential boundedness puts the affine density in [1/2,3/2] a.e. for small |ε|, including the degenerate bound M=0. Centering and reference probability give mass one. The density is positive a.e.; withDensity of its ENNReal image yields the actual probability measure and its a.e. Radon–Nikodym derivative.
steps.lean: The owned actual-law parent proves positivity, normalization and the canonical KL identity; the upper bound is used in its proof, not assumed by the new theorem.

steps.title: Prove finite extended-real KL first
steps.text: The canonical KL is the nonnegative-real image of the compensated integral, which is finite. That establishes KL < ∞ independently of toReal. Nonnegativity of k makes its integral nonnegative, so the real KL then equals the actual real integral.
steps.lean: Use ENNReal.ofReal_lt_top and ENNReal.toReal_ofReal with integral_nonneg_of_ae; toReal ∞ = 0 is never used to justify finiteness.

steps.title: Use the compensated-integral limit
steps.text: At 1, k and its first derivative vanish. Taylor's integral remainder divides by ε² only off zero; the positive segment gives the f² envelope, and the limit is f²/2. The analytic parent proves this scalar coefficient and domination, then passes the integral to the limit.
steps.lean: tendsto_integral_klFun_one_add_mul_div_sq supplies the punctured integral limit; congr' substitutes the eventual real KL identity.

steps.title: Include the exact zero endpoint
steps.text: At ε=0 the density is one, so the tilted law equals μ and its KL is zero. The remainder vanishes there. Combine the punctured quotient limit with the exact endpoint to obtain little-o on the full neighborhood.
steps.lean: withDensity_one, klDiv_self, nhdsNE_sup_pure and Asymptotics.isLittleO_of_tendsto discharge the full-neighborhood conclusion.

units.lean_statement: The result is the conjunction of eventual probability and finite extended-real KL, and a real little-o expansion for that actual law. The probability and finiteness conjunct is not replaced by a real-valued bound.
units.lean_proof: Use the canonical actual-law identity, transfer the independent compensated integral limit, and prove the zero endpoint before converting the vanishing quotient into little-o.
